machine: chapel1: Intel Core i5-10210U (4 cores, 8 threads), 23 GB RAM, Linux, no GPU used
method: silas-bench run --fast --threads 3 under `nice -n 10 taskset -c 1,2,3` (bench/models/run.sh): every model goes through the same dictation path (pieces cut at pauses while the clip plays, the 200 ms tail, the rest at key up, the default dictionary). --fast keeps model time real and simulates the waiting, so the wait after key up is what a real-time run would see on this machine at 3 cores. transcribe.cpp models run in process on its CPU backend with 3 threads; ONNX models run in process through transcribe-rs (onnxruntime's own thread count, held to 3 cores by taskset); whisper.cpp runs as whisper-server with 3 threads on the same cores, its CPU and peak memory added to each row.
